evidence: Cic. Phil. 8.20: tormentīs Mutinam verberāvit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The ancient catapults and ballistae, named from torqueō, twist, for their twisted ropes; Traupman uses the word for modern guns too.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 273.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
